items.title: BusinessWorld PH runs Reuters wire on Gucci's 'Made in China' Drip sneakers breaking with Italian-made tradition
items.summary: Philippine business daily republishes Reuters' report that Gucci's new Demna-designed 'Drip' sneaker (about $980-1,000 in the US, EUR800-820 in Europe) is labelled 'Made in China,' a break from the brand's Italian manufacturing identity. Article carries analyst skepticism: Berenberg warns of tension between provenance and luxury positioning; Milan consultant Simon Whitehouse is quoted directly calling it 'not a good look.' Independent critical-angle wire coverage reaching SEA readers via a national business outlet, not brand-staged content.

items.title: Reuters: Barclays analyst warns Chinese-made Gucci sneakers could deepen 'should we keep buying Gucci' value-proposition debate
items.summary: Original Reuters wire on the Drip sneaker's 'Made in China' label quotes Barclays analyst Carole Madjo flagging customer hesitation about Gucci's pricing versus provenance, and Berenberg analysts warning of tension between the shoe's origin and the brand's luxury repositioning under Demna. Gucci defends the choice citing the manufacturer's 'technological know-how.' T1 wire source carrying substantive independent critical framing, distinct from activation coverage.

items.title: Attack of the Fanboy aggregates social-media backlash to Gucci's 'Made in China' $1,000 sneakers amid 39% three-year revenue drop
items.summary: Consumer-tech/culture outlet frames online reaction to the Drip sneaker's China label as backlash against perceived cost-cutting while retail price stays flat, citing a widely circulated X/Twitter post (Polymarket account) that flagged the story. Notes Gucci's revenue fell roughly 39% between 2023 and 2025, compounding skepticism about whether the premium price is still justified. Discount for aggregation without independently verified engagement counts.

items.title: Esquire Thailand: Gucci names Thai actor PP Krit as its newest brand ambassador
items.summary: Thai edition of Esquire reports Gucci's official announcement of PP Krit (Krit Amnuaydechkorn) as brand ambassador, following his exit from a Balenciaga contract. Descriptive activation coverage of the appointment; included for regional relevance (fourth Thai ambassador after Davika Hoorne, Gulf Kanawut, and prior signings) and because it anchors the fresher fandom coverage of his Milan debut this week (see items 05-06).
